help.intro: After sein an adjective has no ending: Der Tisch ist neu. Before a noun it takes one: ein neuer Tisch, eine neue Lampe, ein neues Haus. This is the first meeting with adjective endings — the full system with all cases comes later in the course and is a real cliff — and it is deliberately small: nominative and accusative only, after ein and after der. Two patterns cover it. After ein, the adjective shows the gender because ein cannot: ein neuER Tisch, eine neuE Lampe, ein neuES Haus (and as an object: einen neuEN Tisch). After der/die/das the article already shows the gender, so the adjective just takes -e: der neue Tisch, die neue Lampe, das neue Haus (and den neuen Tisch as an object). Read them, say them, copy them; understanding why comes later.
help.tips[0].title: After ein: the adjective shows the gender
help.tips[0].text: ein neuer Tisch (m) · eine neue Lampe (f) · ein neues Haus (n). -er, -e, -es echo der, die, das. Object: einen neuen Tisch (m), the rest unchanged.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: That's a good film. I saw a good film.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: She has a red jacket and a fast car.
help.tips[0].trap: English adjectives never change. In German the adjective before a noun always carries an ending; the bare form is a mistake there.
help.tips[0].check.q: Er kauft ein ____ Auto. (das Auto, neu)
help.tips[0].check.why: ein can't show that Auto is neuter, so the adjective does it with -es.
help.tips[0].visual.caption: ein does not show the gender, so the adjective does: -er, -e, -es.
help.tips[0].visual.rows[0].label: the
help.tips[0].visual.rows[1].label: a
help.tips[1].title: After der/die/das: just -e (or -en for a masculine object)
help.tips[1].text: der neue Tisch, die neue Lampe, das neue Haus — the article has done the work, the adjective adds a quiet -e. Object: den neuen Tisch.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Where is the old man? I don't see the old man.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The new house is beautiful. I'm buying the new table.
help.tips[1].check.why: After der/die/das the adjective takes -e, but a masculine object (den) makes it -en.
help.tips[2].title: One strong signal
help.tips[2].text: Either the article shows the gender (der/die/das → adjective takes -e) or the adjective must (ein → adjective takes -er/-e/-es). Never both, never neither. This one idea is the whole adjective-ending system in miniature.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: the article signals — the adjective signals
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: the big house — a big house
help.tips[2].check.why: kleine only has the quiet -e, so the article has to show the gender: das. After ein it would have to be ein kleines Kind.
help.tips[3].title: Plural and the ending -en
help.tips[3].text: die neuen Tische (plural after die → -en). Without article: neue Tische. You will meet these; you don't need to produce them yet.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: I have short hair and blue eyes.
help.tips[3].check.why: In the plural after die, the adjective takes -en.
help.remember[0]: ein + adjective: -er / -e / -es (and -en for a masculine object).
help.remember[1]: der/die/das + adjective: -e (and -en for a masculine object).
help.context.en: I have a new flat! It has a big living room and a small kitchen. The old table doesn't fit, so I'm buying a new table. My nice neighbour gave me a lovely lamp. The interesting book on the table is from her.
help.mistakes[0].why: Before a noun the adjective takes an ending; after ein the masculine takes -er.
help.mistakes[2].why: After die the adjective just takes -e.
help.hook: Say 'a new flat', 'a big kitchen' and 'the old table' with your first adjective endings, all built on one simple idea.
